δηλοῦσθαι ἐκ τοῦ ἐν φόβῳ Χριστοῦ. [v 22, 23] αἱ γυναῖκες τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀνδράσιν
ὑποτασσέσθωσαν ὡς τῷ κυρίῳ· ὅτι ἀνήρ ἐστι κεφαλὴ τῆς γυναικὸς ὡς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς
κεφαλὴ τῆς ἐκκλησίας. πᾶσαν συζυγίαν ἀνδρὸς καὶ γυναικὸς ὁ λόγος οὗτος
σύμβολον εἶναι θέλει Χριστοῦ καὶ ἐκκλησίας· τοῦ μὲν ἀνδρός, εἰ τὰ τοῦ γάμου κατὰ
λόγον οἰκονομεῖ, μιμουμένο<υ> Χριστὸν τὸν τῆς ἐκκλησίας νυμφίον, τῆς δὲ
γυναικός, ἐὰν δεόντως ἀνδρὶ συνοικῇ, ζηλούσης τὴν (ἵν' οὕτως εἴπω) συμβίωσιν
πρὸς τὸν Χριστὸν τῆς ἐκκλησίας. οὕτω γὰρ ὁ ἀνὴρ ἔσται κεφαλὴ τῆς γυναικὸς
ὁμοίως τῷ καὶ τὸν Χριστὸν τῆς ἐκκλησίας. εἰ μέντοιγε μὴ οὕτως συναρμοσθεῖεν
ἀλλήλοις ἀνὴρ καὶ γυνή, οὐκ ἂν λεχθείη ἐπὶ τούτων ὅτι ὅδε τις κεφαλή ἐστι τῆς
γυναικὸς ὡς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς τῆς ἐκκλησίας. φιλοτιμείσθω οὖν ἕκαστος ἀνὴρ εἶναι
πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα ὡς ὁ Χριστὸς πρὸς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, καὶ ἑκάστη πρὸς τὸν ἄνδρα ὡς ἡ
ἐκκλησία πρὸς τὸν Χριστόν· καὶ πάντα δὲ τὰ Χριστοῦ νοείτω καὶ ποιείτω ἀνήρ, καὶ
τὰ τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἡ γυνή. 30 Eph. v24 [ἀλλὰ ὡς ἡ ἐκκλησία ὑποτάσσεται τῷ Χριστῷ,
οὕτως καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες τοῖς ἀνδράσιν ἐν παντί.] [Ὠριγένης φησίν] εἰ οὕτως δεῖ τὰς
γυναῖκας ὑποτάσσεσθαι τοῖς ἀνδράσιν, ὡς ἡ ἐκκλησία ὑποτάσσεται τῷ Χριστῷ, ἁγίως
καὶ ἀπαθῶς καὶ ἀναμαρτήτως δεήσει βιούσας τὰς γυναῖκας ὑποτάσσεσθαι τοῖς
ἀνδράσιν, ὥσπερ ἡ ἐκκλησία ὑποτάσσεται τῷ Χριστῷ ἁγίως καὶ ἀπαθῶς καὶ
ἀναμαρτήτως βιοῦσα. v 27. [ἵνα παραστήσῃ αὐτὸς ἑαυτῷ ἔνδοξον τὴν ἐκκλησίαν μὴ
ἔχουσαν σπῖλον ἢ ῥυτίδα ἤ τι τῶν τοιούτων ἀλλ' ἵνα ᾖ ἁγία καὶ ἄμωμος.] σπῖλοι δέ
εἰσιν οἷον φακοὶ γινόμενοι ἐπὶ τοῦ σώματος καὶ μελανίαι καὶ ἀλφοὶ καὶ μυρμηκίαι·
τούτων γὰρ περιαιρεθέντων ὡραιοτέρα γένοιτ' ἂν γυνή· καὶ τὰ ἀνάλογον αὐτοῖς
νοείσθω γινόμενα καὶ περὶ τὴν ψυχήν, ἅτινα οὐδενός ἐστιν ἢ τοῦ Λόγου περιελεῖν,
ἵνα παραστήσῃ ἑαυτῷ, φησί, τὴν ἰδίαν νύμφην μὴ ἔχουσαν σπῖλον ἢ ῥυτίδα ἤ τι τῶν
τοιούτων ἀλλ' ἵνα ᾖ ἁγία καὶ ἄμωμος. ῥυτίδες δὲ σημεῖόν εἰσι γήρως· οὕτως εἴ τις
ἴχνη τοῦ παλαιοῦ ἐπιμένοι ἔχων μὴ ἀεὶ ἀνακαινούμενο , ῥερυτιδῶσθαι ἂν λέγοιτο
κατὰ τὴν ψυχήν. [ 31] ἀντὶ τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα
καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν. παρατηρητέον, ὥσπερ καὶ ἐν ἄλλοις πεποιήκαμεν,
ὅτι πολλάκις οὐκ αὐταῖς λέξεσιν ἐκτίθενται τὴν παλαιὰν γραφὴν οἱ τὴν καινὴν
διαθήκην γράφοντες. καὶ περὶ μὲν τούτου ἐν μὲν τῇ Γενέσει οὕτω γέγραπται ἕνεκεν
τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπο τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ
προ κολληθή εται πρὸ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔ ονται οἱ δύο εἰ άρκα μίαν, ἐνθάδε
δὲ ἀντὶ τοῦ ἕνεκεν τούτου πεποίηκεν ὁ Παῦλος ἀντὶ τούτου, παραλέλοιπέν τε τὸ
μετὰ τὸν πατέρα εἰρημένον αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ μετὰ τὴν μητέρα δεύτερον εἰρημένον
αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ προ κολληθή εται πρὸ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ. 31 Eph. vi1–3 τὰ
τέκνα, ὑπακούετε τοῖς γονεῦσιν ὑμῶν ἐν Κυρίῳ, τοῦτο γάρ ἐστι δίκαιον· τίμα τὸν
πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἐντολὴ πρώτη ἐν ἐπαγγελίᾳ, ἵνα εὖ σοι
γένηται καὶ ἔσῃ μακροχρόνιος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. [Ὠριγένης φησίν] ἀμφίβολόν ἐστι τὸ
ῥητόν· ἤτοι γὰρ τοῖς ἐν Κυρίῳ γονεῦσιν χρὴ ὑπακούειν τὰ τέκνα, ἢ ἐν Κυρίῳ δεῖ
ὑπακούειν τὰ τέκνα τοῖς γονεῦσιν. καὶ οὐδετέραν γε τῶν ἐκδοχῶν ἀποδοκιμαστέον·
τοῖς τε γὰρ ἐν Κυρίῳ γονεῦσιν, ὁποῖος ὁ Παῦλος ἦν Κορινθίων, ὑπακουστέον, καὶ
τοῖς κατὰ σάρκα γονεῦσιν ὑπακουστέον, ἀλλὰ ἐν Κυρίῳ, προστάττουσιν οὐκ ἐναντία
τῷ τοῦ Κυρίου βουλήματι. δίκαιον δὲ τὸ ὑπακούειν καθ' ἑκάτερον. ἅμα δὲ καὶ
σημειώσῃ πρὸς ἑτεροδόξους διαχωρίζοντας δίκαιον Θεὸν ἀπὸ ἀγαθοῦ, ὅτι τοῖς
μαθηταῖς τοῦ ὥς φασιν ἀγαθοῦ προστάσσει τὸ (ὡς ἂν ἐκεῖνοι λέγοιεν) πρόσταγμα
τοῦ ἑτέρου Θεοῦ· εἴγε ὁ ἕτερος δίκαιός ἐστιν, καὶ φησὶν ὁ Παῦλος δίκαιον εἶναι τὸ τὰ
τέκνα ὑπακούειν τοῖς γονεῦσιν ἐν Κυρίῳ ἢ ἐν Κυρίῳ ὑπακούειν τοῖς γονεῦσιν. τὸ δὲ
ῥητὸν εἴληπται ἀπὸ τῆς Ἐξόδου, οὕτως ἔχον τίμα τὸν πατέρα ου καὶ τὴν μητέρα ου
ἵνα εὖ οι γένηται καὶ ἵνα μακροχρόνιο γένῃ ἐπὶ τῆ γῆ ἧ Κύριο ὁ Θεό ου δίδω ί οι.
καὶ ἐνθάδε δὲ ἐκτιθέμενος ὁ ἀπόστολος τὴν λέξιν παρα λέλοιπεν τὸ (μετὰ τὴν
μητέρα) ου, καὶ πεποίηκεν ἀντὶ τοῦ καὶ ἵνα μακροχρόνιο γένῃ καὶ ἔσῃ
μακροχρόνιος, παραλέλοιπέν τε μετὰ τὸ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς τὸ ἧ Κύριο ὁ Θεό ου δίδω ί οι.
ἔστι δὲ ἡ ἐντολὴ πέμπτη τῆς ∆εκαλόγου· διὸ ζητητέον πῶς δεῖ ἐκλαβεῖν τὸ ἥτις ἐστὶν
ἐντολὴ πρώτη, πρώτης εἰρημένης ἐντολῆς τὸ οὐκ ἔ ονταί οι θεοὶ ἕτεροι πλὴν ἐμοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: ... to be shown from the "in fear of Christ". Eph 5:22-23: let the wives be subjected to their own husbands as to the Lord; because a man is head of the woman as also Christ is head of the church. This saying wishes every yoking of man and woman to be a symbol of Christ and church: of the man, if he manages the things of the marriage according to reason, imitating Christ the bridegroom of the church; and of the woman, if she dwells with a man as is due, emulating the (that I may speak so) living-together of the church toward Christ. For thus the man will be head of the woman similarly to the Christ also being so of the church. If however man and woman should not be fitted together thus to one another, it would not be said in their case that this one is head of the woman as also Christ of the church. Therefore let each man be ambitious to be toward the woman as the Christ toward the church, and each woman toward the man as the church toward the Christ; and let the man think and do all the things of Christ, and the woman those of the church. Eph 5:24 lemma: but as the church is subjected to Christ, so also the wives to the husbands in everything. [Origen says] If the wives must be subjected to the husbands thus, as the church is subjected to Christ, it will be needed that the wives, living holily and passionlessly and sinlessly, be subjected to the husbands, as the church is subjected to Christ living holily and passionlessly and sinlessly. Eph 5:27 lemma: that he himself may present to himself glorious the church not having stain or wrinkle or any of such things, but that it may be holy and blameless. Stains are such as lentil-spots occurring on the body and black patches and white leprous spots and warts; for when these are removed a woman would become more beautiful; and let the things analogous to them be understood as occurring also about the soul, which it is of no one except the Word to remove, that he may present to himself, it says, his own bride not having stain or wrinkle or any such thing but that she be holy and blameless. And wrinkles are a sign of old age; so if someone should keep having traces of the old, not always being renewed, he would be said to have become wrinkled according to the soul. Eph 5:31: in return for this a man will leave the father and the mother and the two will be into one flesh. One must observe, as we have done also in other places, that often not in the very words do those writing the new covenant set out the old writing. And about this in Genesis it is written thus: on account of this a man will leave his father and his mother and will be glued to his wife and the two will be into one flesh; but here in place of the "on account of this" Paul has made "in return for this", and he has left out the "his" said after the father and the "his" said second after the mother, and also the "will be glued to his wife". Eph 6:1-3 lemma: the children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is just; honor your father and the mother, which is a first command in promise, that it may become well for you and you will be long-timed upon the earth. [Origen says] The saying is double-meaning: for either to the parents in the Lord the children must listen, or in the Lord the children must listen to the parents. And neither of the acceptations is to be rejected: for both to the parents in the Lord, of which sort Paul was of the Corinthians, one must listen, and to the parents according to flesh one must listen, but in the Lord, when they command things not contrary to the wish of the Lord. And listening is just according to each. At the same time you will mark also, toward heterodox people dividing a just God from a good one, that to the disciples of the, as they say, good one he orders the (as those would say) command of the other God; if indeed the other is just, and Paul says that it is just for the children to listen to the parents in the Lord or in the Lord to listen to the parents. And the saying has been taken from Exodus, holding thus: honor your father and your mother that it may become well for you and that you may become long-timed upon the land which Lord your God gives to you. And here too the apostle, setting out the phrase, has left out the "your" (after the mother), and in place of "and that you may become long-timed" he has made "and you will be long-timed", and he has left out after the "upon the earth" the "which Lord your God gives you". And the command is fifth of the Decalogue; wherefore one must seek how one must take the "which is first command", the first command having been said: there will not be to you other gods except me.
pass_b_english: is what is meant by "in the fear of Christ."

"Wives, be subject to your own husbands as to the Lord; for the husband is the head of the wife, as Christ also is the head of the church" (Ephesians 5:22-23). This saying wants every union of husband and wife to be a symbol of Christ and the church. The husband, if he orders the life of the marriage by reason, imitates Christ, the bridegroom of the church; the wife, if she lives with her husband as she should, strives to match the church's (if I may put it so) shared life with Christ. For so the husband will be the head of the wife, just as Christ is of the church. But if husband and wife are not joined to each other in this way, it could not be said of them that this man is the head of his wife as Christ also is of the church. So let each husband make it his ambition to be toward his wife as Christ is toward the church, and each wife toward her husband as the church is toward Christ. Let the husband think and do all that belongs to Christ, and the wife all that belongs to the church.

"But as the church is subject to Christ, so also wives to their husbands in everything" (Ephesians 5:24). Origen says: If wives must be subject to their husbands in the way the church is subject to Christ, then wives will have to live holy lives, free of passion and without sin, as they are subject to their husbands, just as the church is subject to Christ while living a holy life, free of passion and without sin.

"That he might present the church to himself in glory, having no spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that it might be holy and blameless" (Ephesians 5:27). Spots are things like the freckles that form on the body, dark patches, white blotches and warts; once these are taken away, a woman would be more beautiful. Let us understand that corresponding things form on the soul too, and it belongs to no one but the Word to take them away, "that he might present to himself," it says, his own bride, "having no spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she might be holy and blameless." Wrinkles are a sign of old age. So if someone kept bearing traces of the old self and was not always being renewed, he might be said to be wrinkled in his soul.

"For this a man shall leave father and mother, and the two shall become one flesh" (Ephesians 5:31). We should note, as we have done elsewhere, that the writers of the New Testament often do not set out the old Scripture in its exact words. On this point Genesis has: "For this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh" (Genesis 2:24). But here, in place of "for this reason," Paul has put "for this"; and he has left out the "his" that comes after "father" and the second "his" that comes after "mother," as well as "and be joined to his wife."

"Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is just. 'Honor your father and mother'—which is the first commandment with a promise—'that it may be well with you, and you will live long on the earth'" (Ephesians 6:1-3). Origen says: The text is ambiguous. Either children must obey parents who are in the Lord, or children must obey their parents in the Lord. And neither reading should be rejected. Parents in the Lord, as Paul was to the Corinthians, must be obeyed; and parents according to the flesh must be obeyed too, but in the Lord, when they command nothing contrary to the Lord's will. In either sense, obeying is just.

At the same time, you will note this against the heterodox who separate a just God from a good one: to the disciples of the one they call "the good," he gives what they would call a command of the other God, if indeed that other God is the just one; and Paul says that it is just for children to obey their parents in the Lord, or to obey their parents in the Lord. The text is taken from Exodus, which reads: "Honor your father and your mother, that it may be well with you, and that you may live long on the land which the Lord your God gives you" (Exodus 20:12). Here too, as he sets out the words, the apostle has left out the "your" after "mother"; in place of "and that you may live long" he has put "and you will live long"; and after "on the earth" he has left out "which the Lord your God gives you." Now this commandment is the fifth of the Ten Commandments. So we must ask how to take "which is the first commandment," when the first commandment given is, "You shall have no other gods besides me" (Exodus 20:3).

choices.english: you will note this against the heterodox
choices.why: A full sentence addressed to the reader, as in the Greek; the old English turned it into a heading-like label.
In the lemma and the argument alike, so that Origen's point against those who separate the 'just' God from the 'good' one stays visible.
Two Greek phrases of the same meaning; English cannot show the word change exactly, so two close English phrases stand for them.

choices.english: on the earth (Ephesians) / on the land (Exodus)
choices.why: Same Greek; English Bibles distinguish them, and Origen's comparison is about the words that follow.
